decision.decision_reason:
Both iterations have collectively returned a rich, multi-source, multi-date evidence set that covers all target fields for the August 2025 NYC Legionnaires' disease outbreak. The stopping conditions are met on two independent grounds: (1) the max_iterations bound of 2 has been reached, and (2) the evidence is substantively sufficient — additional queries are very unlikely to yield materially new data points beyond what is already captured.

Specifically, the accepted candidate pool now includes:
• Multiple dated NYC DOHMH primary press releases on nyc.gov spanning the full outbreak arc: July 28 (HAN Alert #4, 5 confirmed cases, 0 deaths), July 30 (22 cases, 1 death), August 4 (second update), August 14 (third update, 101 cases, 4 deaths, 11/12 towers remediated), August 26 (113+ cases, 6 deaths, 7 hospitalized), and August 29 (cluster closed, 7 deaths) — providing dated snapshots for cases_confirmed, deaths, and hospitalizations across the entire window.
• NYC Mayor's Office transcripts (August 14 press conference, August 29 closing briefing) corroborating DOHMH figures with direct quotes.
• NYS Health Care Providers EP Alert (August 15) with independent corroboration of 99 confirmed cases and 17 hospitalized as of August 15.
• Goldberg Segalla legal/public health summary (August 26–27 snapshot: 113+ confirmed, 6 deaths, 7 hospitalized) — secondary but well-sourced.
• ABC7NY news article (sixth death, 111 cases) with NYS DOH review announcement.
• VaccineAdvisor/HealthDay article (fourth death, 101 cases, August 14 snapshot).
• BMJ article (five deaths, 14 hospitalized as of August 20).
• Respiratory-therapy.com aggregator with sixth death (August 27 update) and Bronx condominium isolated cases note.
• Manhattan Borough President public health alert page (corroborating official outbreak declaration).
• CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu, 1 result in iteration 2) — likely contains a structured outbreak summary.
• NBC New York, CBS News, Contagion Live, Infectious Disease Advisor — additional news corroboration.

All target fields are addressable: disease (Legionnaires' disease), country (USA), subnational_location (New York State), locality (Central Harlem, ZIP codes 10027/10030/10035/10037/10039), date_reported (multiple dated snapshots from July 28 through August 29), cases_confirmed (5 → 22 → 99 → 101 → 113+ → final), deaths (0 → 1 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7), hospitalizations (17 on Aug 15; 14 on Aug 20; 7 on Aug 26), source_url (multiple nyc.gov primary URLs plus secondary sources), source_type (official_public_health_agency, news_and_situation_report), and evidence_quote (direct quotes available from DOHMH press releases and Mayor's Office transcripts).

The Bronx condominium cluster (iter2_q4) did not surface as a distinct August 2025 event with independent case counts — consistent with the prior warning that it likely predates the task window or represents background surveillance. No new cluster requiring separate data rows was confirmed.

The CDC NNDSS gap (no August 2025 NYC-specific NNDSS table) is expected and acceptable — NNDSS data for August 2025 would not be finalized or published at this time. The ProMED post appeared in domain counts but was not summarized; given the richness of primary DOHMH sources, its absence does not create a material gap.

No further queries would meaningfully improve coverage of the target fields within the task window.
decision.coverage_assessment: COMPREHENSIVE. All target fields are covered by at least one, and most by multiple, accepted source candidates. Dated case/death/hospitalization snapshots span the full August 2025 window (Aug 1–29) from primary DOHMH sources. The outbreak arc from initial cluster declaration through closure is fully documented. Locality is resolved to Central Harlem ZIP codes. The final confirmed totals (7 deaths, 130+ cases by closure) are anchored to the August 29 DOHMH primary press release. Intermediate snapshots provide granular time-series data for the entire month.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: STRONG. Sources span: (1) NYC DOHMH primary press releases and HAN alerts (nyc.gov — highest trust, multiple URLs); (2) NYC Mayor's Office transcripts (nyc.gov — corroborating official figures with direct quotes); (3) NYS Health Care Providers EP Alert (nyshcp.org — independent state-level corroboration); (4) Manhattan Borough President official page (manhattanbp.nyc.gov — official NYC government corroboration); (5) Peer-reviewed/academic outlet (BMJ — international medical journal with DOHMH-sourced figures); (6) Academic public health aggregator (CIDRAP — University of Minnesota); (7) Multiple established news outlets (ABC7NY, NBC New York, CBS News, VaccineAdvisor/HealthDay); (8) Legal/public health analysis (Goldberg Segalla — secondary but well-cited); (9) Clinical/professional aggregators (Respiratory Therapy, Infectious Disease Advisor, Contagion Live). No single source type dominates; official primary sources are well-represented.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: HIGH. The primary evidence chain runs through nyc.gov (DOHMH press releases and HAN alerts) — the authoritative source for NYC Legionnaires' disease surveillance. All key numerical claims (case counts, death tolls, hospitalization figures) are traceable to DOHMH primary sources or direct Mayor's Office transcripts. Secondary sources (news, aggregators) consistently cite DOHMH as their source, providing corroboration without introducing independent unverifiable claims. The BMJ article adds international peer-reviewed validation. The NYS EP Alert provides independent state-level corroboration of the August 15 snapshot. No significant trust concerns remain; the duplicate URL issue from search results is a search-engine artifact, not a data quality problem.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: EXCELLENT FIT. Disease: Legionnaires' disease — confirmed across all sources. Location: New York City, specifically Central Harlem (Manhattan borough), ZIP codes 10027, 10030, 10035, 10037, 10039 — precise sub-city locality established. Time window: The outbreak began in late July 2025 (first DOHMH alert July 28) and was declared closed August 29, 2025 — the vast majority of cases, deaths, and hospitalizations fall squarely within the August 1–31, 2025 task window. The July 28–30 pre-window data points (5 confirmed cases, 1 death) provide useful baseline context but are clearly pre-window. All August 1–29 snapshots are within scope.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: STRONG. The final death count of 7 (August 29 DOHMH closure press release) is corroborated by the Mayor's quote in the same press release. The intermediate counts (4 deaths/101 cases on Aug 14; 5 deaths on Aug 18–19; 6 deaths/111 cases on Aug 26–27; 7 deaths at closure Aug 29) form a consistent, non-contradictory time series across DOHMH primary sources, news outlets, and the NYS EP Alert. The 99 confirmed cases / 17 hospitalized figure from the NYS EP Alert (Aug 15) is consistent with the DOHMH Aug 14 snapshot of 101 cases (slight lag in state reporting). No material contradictions between sources were identified.
